title_en: Jiangsu Gaoke Seed Technology Co., Ltd. v. Nantong Grain and Cotton Original Seed Farm — dispute over the right to claim compensation for a new plant variety
ruling_gist_en: For plant new varieties, the system of "early publication and deferred examination" is implemented. After the grant of the variety right, if the variety right holder claims, in accordance with Article 33 of the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties, payment of royalties from any entity or individual that, without the permission of the applicant, produces or sells the propagating material of the authorized variety for commercial purposes during the period from the publication date of the plant new variety application to the announcement date of the grant, the people's court may reasonably determine the amount by comprehensively considering factors such as the license fee for the exploitation of the relevant plant new variety, the type and value of the variety, and the scale of the operator's business.

full_text_en:
Jiangsu Gaoke Seed Technology Co., Ltd. v. Nantong Grain and Cotton Original Seed Farm — dispute over right of recourse for plant new variety

Ruling Summary

The system of "early publication, delayed examination" is implemented for new varieties of plants. After the variety right is granted, where the variety right holder claims, in accordance with Article 33 of the Regulations on the Protection of New Varieties of Plants, that any entity or individual that, without the permission of the applicant, produces or sells propagation material of the authorized variety for commercial purposes during the period from the date of publication of the application for the new plant variety to the date of announcement of the grant of the right shall pay a usage fee, the people's court may reasonably determine the fee by comprehensively considering factors such as the implementation license fee for the involved new plant variety, the type and value of the variety, and the business scale of the implementer.

Plaintiff: Jiangsu Gaoke Seed Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at Heshun Road, Huai'an Economic and Technological Development Zone, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Sun Zhonglin, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Defendant: Nantong Grain and Cotton Original Seed Farm, domiciled at Xue Yao Village South End, Guo Yuan Town, Rugao City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Guo Xijun, Director of the farm. (Changed to Wu Guohua during the second instance.)

The plaintiff, Jiangsu Gaoke Seed Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gaoke Seed Company), filed a lawsuit with the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court against the defendant, Nantong Grain and Cotton Original Seed Farm (hereinafter referred to as Nantong Original Seed Farm), for a dispute over the right of recourse for a new plant variety.

The plaintiff, Gaoke Seed Company, alleged: The rice variety "Nan Jing 9108" was granted a new plant variety right on May 1, 2015, with variety right number CNA20101060.9. The variety right holder, the Jiangsu Academy of Agricultural Sciences, authorized the plaintiff to exclusively implement the new plant variety right for "Nan Jing 9108," to produce and sell rice seeds of "Nan Jing 9108," and to have the right to seek recourse against any entity or individual that produced or sold propagation material of the variety before the grant of the right for "Nan Jing 9108." The defendant, Nantong Original Seed Farm, produced and sold propagation material of the variety without authorization before the grant of the new plant variety right for "Nan Jing 9108." Therefore, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit, requesting the court to order the defendant to pay the plaintiff a usage fee of RMB 300,000 for the new rice variety "Nan Jing 9108."

The defendant, Nantong Original Seed Farm, argued: 1. It did not infringe the plaintiff Gaoke Seed Company's new plant variety right. The Jiangsu Academy of Agricultural Sciences only obtained the new plant variety right for the involved rice variety "Nan Jing 9108" on May 1, 2015, but Nantong Original Seed Farm only sold 43 jin (1 jin = 0.5 kg) of "Nan Jing 9108" rice from March 16, 2015 to March 20, 2015 (all retail, unpackaged), at which time Gaoke Seed Company had not yet been granted the new plant variety right for the involved "Nan Jing 9108" rice. Therefore, Nantong Original Seed Farm did not infringe the new plant variety right for the involved rice. 2. Gaoke Seed Company's request for Nantong Original Seed Farm to pay a usage fee of RMB 300,000 for the new rice variety "Nan Jing 9108" lacks factual and legal basis. All the "Nan Jing 9108" rice seeds owned by Nantong Original Seed Farm have been confiscated, and only 43 jin were sold before that. Gaoke Seed Company also cannot prove the establishment of its RMB 300,000 usage fee. The defendant requested the dismissal of the plaintiff's claims.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court found the following facts at first instance:

On December 10, 2010, the Jiangsu Academy of Agricultural Sciences applied for new plant variety right protection for the variety "Ning 9108." On March 1, 2011, the application passed the preliminary examination and was announced. On April 10, 2013, the variety passed the examination at the 53rd meeting of the Crop Variety Approval Committee of Jiangsu Province and was approved. In 2014, the variety was renamed "Nan Jing 9108" and announced. On May 1, 2015, the variety was granted a new plant variety right and announced, with variety right number CNA20101060.9, and new plant variety right certificate number 20155100.

On April 7, 2011, the variety right holder, Jiangsu Academy of Agricultural Sciences, and the plaintiff, Gaoke Seed Company, entered into an "Exclusive Implementation License Contract for Ning 9108 Rice Variety." The parties agreed: 1. The Jiangsu Academy of Agricultural Sciences licensed the "Ning 9108" rice variety it owned to Gaoke Seed Company for implementation. 2. The license method was an exclusive implementation license, and the license scope was the suitable planting area approved for the variety. 3. The license fee was RMB 4,500,000, payable in three installments, etc. On April 14, 2011, December 9, 2012, July 1, 2014, and December 8, 2014, Gaoke Seed Company remitted RMB 4,500,000 to the account of the Jiangsu Academy of Agricultural Sciences in four installments, and the Jiangsu Academy of Agricultural Sciences issued invoices to Gaoke Seed Company.

On May 1, 2015, the Jiangsu Academy of Agricultural Sciences issued an "Authorization Letter," authorizing the plaintiff, Gaoke Seed Company, to exclusively implement the new plant variety right for "Nan Jing 9108" and to produce and sell rice seeds of "Nan Jing 9108." Any acts by other entities or individuals of producing, packaging, and selling rice seeds of "Nan Jing 9108" without authorization constituted infringement, and Gaoke Seed Company had the right to pursue the legal liability of the infringer; Gaoke Seed Company also had the right to seek recourse against any entity or individual that produced or sold propagation material of the variety before the grant of the new plant variety right for "Nan Jing 9108."

On July 3, 2015, the Rugao City Agriculture Committee issued an Administrative Penalty Decision (No. (Seeds) Penalty [2015] 01) to the defendant, Nantong Original Seed Farm. The decision found that Nantong Original Seed Farm mainly produced seeds on behalf of seed companies with production and operation qualifications or produced high-quality rice for rice mills. In 2014, there were reports that the party concerned was suspected of producing and selling rice seeds such as "Nan Jing 9108" in unmarked bags without a license. Upon investigation, in 2014, the party concerned planted "Nan Jing 9108" and others as experimental field rice, of which "Nan Jing 9108" was not processed or screened, with 2,227 jin stored in the warehouse. The farm headquarters used 1,000 jin to process 723 jin of rice. The warehouse keeper, Xue, sold 43 jin as seeds at a price of RMB 3.5/jin, and the existing inventory was 1,184 jin. The administrative penalty decision confiscated the 1,184 jin of "Nan Jing 9108" and the illegal gains, and imposed a fine. Nantong Original Seed Farm performed the administrative penalty decision.

The issue in dispute at first instance: Whether the plaintiff Gaoke Seed Company's claim for a usage fee for the involved new plant variety right should be supported.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held at first instance:

First, based on the contract entered into by both parties, the payment vouchers of the plaintiff Gaoke Seed Company, the invoices issued by the variety right holder, and the authorization letter issued by the variety right holder, it could be proved that Gaoke Seed Company was authorized to implement the involved "Nan Jing 9108" variety right and to file the relevant lawsuit to protect its exclusive implementation right and right of recourse.

Second, the "Nan Jing 9108" variety passed the preliminary examination and was announced on March 1, 2011, and was granted the new plant variety right on May 1, 2015. The period between these two dates is the period during which Gaoke Seed Company claims the right of recourse. The administrative penalty decision of the Rugao City Agriculture Committee found that the defendant, Nantong Original Seed Farm, planted a certain number of mu (1 mu = 0.0667 hectares) of "Nan Jing 9108" rice seeds in 2014, sold them externally in March 2015 in unmarked bags and other packaging forms, and was reported and subjected to the administrative penalty of the Rugao City Agriculture Committee. Nantong Original Seed Farm performed the content of the administrative penalty decision and acknowledged the above facts. Therefore, the existing evidence could prove that Nantong Original Seed Farm produced and sold propagation material of the involved "Nan Jing 9108" variety for commercial purposes during the period from the announcement of the preliminary examination to the grant of the variety right.

Third, the defendant, Nantong Original Seed Farm, should bear corresponding civil liability. Nantong Original Seed Farm produced and sold propagation material of the new plant variety "Nan Jing 9108" for commercial purposes without the permission of the relevant right holder, and should pay the corresponding fee to the plaintiff, Gaoke Seed Company, to compensate for the losses it suffered. Gaoke Seed Company claimed to calculate and determine the amount of compensation based on one year's license fee as the variety usage fee, and provided evidence such as the implementation license contract, payment vouchers, and invoices. The court held that: First, Gaoke Seed Company was authorized to implement the involved "Nan Jing 9108" variety and paid a license fee of RMB 4,500,000, which is equivalent to an average annual payment of RMB 300,000 within the 15-year protection period for the new plant variety right. Second, from the perspective of the license method, Gaoke Seed Company actually obtained the exclusive right and paid the corresponding consideration, obtaining a legal status similar to that of the variety right holder. Third, although the "Regulations on the Protection of New Varieties of Plants of the PRC" and other relevant laws do not specifically stipulate how to calculate the recourse fee, the nature of the involved acts of Nantong Original Seed Farm is characterized as unauthorized production or sale for commercial purposes, which is similar to the unauthorized production or sale for commercial purposes after the grant of the right, i.e., an act similar to infringement of a new plant variety right. The opposite lawful act is the authorized production or sale for commercial purposes, where the license method may be a general license or other forms of license. Therefore, with reference to Article 6 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of New Varieties of Plants, the method and standard for calculating damages claimed by Gaoke Seed Company have a reasonable basis.

Accordingly, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 33 of the Regulations on the Protection of New Varieties of Plants of the PRC, rendered a judgment on September 7, 2016:

The defendant, Nantong Original Seed Farm, shall pay the plaintiff, Gaoke Seed Company, a recourse fee of RMB 300,000 for the new rice variety "Nan Jing 9108."

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, Nantong Original Seed Farm, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, appealed to the Jiangsu High People's Court, alleging: 1. The original trial judgment erred in finding that the appellee Gaoke Seed Company had standing. The right of recourse provided for in the Regulations on the Protection of New Varieties of Plants can only be exercised by the variety right holder, and a licensee cannot exercise the right of recourse. The authorization letter submitted by Gaoke Seed Company did not authorize it to file a recourse lawsuit in its own name. This case is also not a dispute over infringement of a new plant variety right, and the relevant judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the trial of disputes over new plant variety rights is not applicable. 2. The first instance judgment ordering Nantong Original Seed Farm to pay a recourse fee of RMB 300,000 lacks legal basis. 1. The Regulations on the Protection of New Varieties of Plants and relevant judicial interpretations have no clear provisions on the recourse fee. This case is not a dispute over infringement of a new plant variety right, and the first instance court's treatment of it as similar to an infringement of a new plant variety right has no legal basis. 2. The license fee should be calculated from the date of signing the contract in April 2011, plus the 15-year protection period after the grant of the right on May 1, 2015, totaling 19 years. The first instance judgment's calculation of the average usage fee based on the 15-year protection period is clearly inappropriate. 3. Nantong Original Seed Farm did not produce or sell for commercial purposes, but for scientific experiments. After the Rugao City Agriculture Committee organized an investigation, it promptly corrected the mistake, causing no social impact or damage to Gaoke Seed Company. At the same time, the sales occurred before the grant of the involved variety right, and the loss and standard calculated by Gaoke Seed Company have no reasonable basis.

The appellee, Gaoke Seed Company, argued: 1. The first instance judgment's finding that Gaoke Seed Company had standing was correct. After the involved rice variety "Nan Jing 9108" passed the approval of the Jiangsu Provincial Crop Variety Approval Committee, Gaoke Seed Company entered into an exclusive implementation license contract with the variety right applicant, the Jiangsu Academy of Agricultural Sciences. Before the grant of the variety right, Gaoke Seed Company had already produced and sold seeds of the involved rice variety and published a rights protection statement, warning the public not to produce or sell without authorization. After the grant of the right, the variety right holder formally authorized Gaoke Seed Company to exercise the right of recourse. Therefore, Gaoke Seed Company has the right to exercise the right of recourse. 2. The amount of the recourse fee determined by the first instance judgment is not improper. The protection period for new plant varieties is 15 years, but in practice, the actual time of application in the market is only 3-5 years, and for well-performing varieties, at most 8-10 years. Especially in Jiangsu, where rice varieties are abundant, new varieties emerge one after another, and the variety renewal cycle is short. In this case, calculating the license fee based on the 15-year protection period actually benefits the appellant, Nantong Original Seed Farm, especially since its production and sales were not limited to one year.

The Jiangsu High People's Court, upon second instance, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The issues in dispute at second instance were: 1. Whether the appellee Gaoke Seed Company had standing in this case; 2. Whether the appellant Nantong Original Seed Farm produced and sold the propagation material of the involved "Nan Jing 9108" variety for commercial purposes; 3. Whether the first instance judgment's determination of the usage fee of RMB 300,000 payable by Nantong Original Seed Farm was appropriate.

The Jiangsu High People's Court held at second instance:

1. The appellee Gaoke Seed Company had standing in this case. The right of recourse is a civil right enjoyed by the variety right holder. Its voluntary authorization for Gaoke Seed Company to exercise the right of recourse does not violate any prohibitive provisions of laws or administrative regulations. Therefore, as the licensee under the exclusive implementation license contract, Gaoke Seed Company may independently file a lawsuit for the dispute over the right of recourse for the involved new plant variety, and it has standing.

2. The appellant Nantong Original Seed Farm, without permission, produced and sold the propagation material of the involved "Nan Jing 9108" variety for commercial purposes. Nantong Original Seed Farm is a state-owned enterprise legal person specializing in seed production, not a farmer who self-propagates and self-uses crops. The 2014 trial plan did not include the involved "Nan Jing 9108" variety, and its claim that it planted the involved variety in 2014 for experimental purposes lacked sufficient basis. Moreover, in 2015, Nantong Original Seed Farm sold the "Nan Jing 9108" it produced on the market, and this act itself had a commercial purpose. Therefore, based on the existing evidence in this case, it could be determined that Nantong Original Seed Farm produced and sold the propagation material of the involved "Nan Jing 9108" for commercial purposes.

3. The amount of the usage fee for the provisional protection period that the appellee Gaoke Seed Company may recover can be reasonably determined by reference to the involved implementation license fee. The Regulations on the Protection of New Varieties of Plants of the PRC provide that the period from the date of announcement of the preliminary examination to the date of grant of the variety right is the provisional protection period for new plant varieties. After the variety right is granted, the right holder may seek recourse against any entity or individual that, without permission, produced or sold propagation material of the authorized variety for commercial purposes during that period. However, the Regulations on the Protection of New Varieties of Plants of the PRC and other relevant laws have no clear and specific provisions on the nature of such acts committed during the provisional protection period or on how the implementer shall bear civil liability. In judicial practice, variety right holders usually claim to pay the variety usage fee for the provisional protection period by reference to the implementation license fee for the new plant variety. In this regard, the second instance judgment held that the prerequisite for provisional protection is that the variety is granted, i.e., only after the variety is granted can the previously published variety be given extended protection. Therefore, after the variety is granted, entities or individuals that, without permission, produced or sold propagation material of the authorized variety for commercial purposes during the provisional protection period shall pay the corresponding usage fee to the variety right holder. And according to the variety right holder's claim, determining the usage fee for that period by reference to the license method is consistent with the legislative spirit of encouraging innovation in seed industry science and technology and the cultivation of new plant varieties, and is also relatively fair and reasonable. In this case, the specific amount of the usage fee for the involved variety needs to be determined by comprehensively considering the following factors.

First, according to the terms of the involved exclusive implementation license agreement, the total implementation license fee for the "Nan Jing 9108" variety right was RMB 4,500,000, and the appellee Gaoke Seed Company paid the above amount as agreed. From the date of signing the involved license contract to the end of the protection period for the variety right, the license term was 19 years. Calculated over 19 years, the average annual implementation license fee was approximately RMB 240,000. The first instance judgment's calculation of the average annual implementation license fee based on the protection period of 15 years was inappropriate and should be corrected. However, the amount agreed in the implementation license fee is only a reference for determining the usage fee during the provisional protection period. Factors such as the type of new plant variety right and the market application period also need to be considered. It is not appropriate to simply calculate the average annual implementation license fee standard based on the agreed 19-year license term and then determine the amount of the usage fee for one year during the provisional protection period.

Second, the evidence provided by the appellee Gaoke Seed Company, including the land use right certificate and business premises certificate of the appellant Nantong Original Seed Farm, showed that the land area of Nantong Original Seed Farm was approximately 3,500 mu. As a state-owned enterprise legal person specializing in seed production, all its land was state-owned agricultural land. Nantong Original Seed Farm was fully capable of providing relevant evidence to prove the area and use of its land. The data on cultivated land area it provided during the second instance was provided unilaterally by itself. In the absence of sufficient evidence, based solely on its own statement, it could not be determined that the actual arable land for rice planting was only 1,033 mu. At the same time, according to the production and processing agreement provided by Nantong Original Seed Farm, it could be determined that in 2014, Nantong Original Seed Farm produced and processed 500-600 mu of Changnongjing 8 for Nantong Zhongjiang Seed Company and 320 mu of Huaidao 5 for Rugao Baisui Rice Mill, but Nantong Original Seed Farm failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove what crops were planted on the remaining more than 2,000 mu of land. Accordingly, Gaoke Seed Company's assertion that Nantong Original Seed Farm planted a large area of the involved "Nan Jing 9108" propagation material had a relatively high degree of credibility.

Finally, it should be particularly pointed out that the involved variety is japonica rice, and the cultivation of new japonica rice varieties requires efforts in improvement and innovation in many aspects such as increasing yield and improving taste quality, which has cost scientific and technological workers great effort. At the same time, the quality of grain seeds is related to the safety of agricultural production, the vital interests of farmers, and the life and health of the people, which are major issues related to people's livelihoods. Therefore, China implements a seed license system and strictly supervises and controls the cultivation, source, quality, production, and operation of seeds. In this case, the appellant Nantong Original Seed Farm, without the permission of the variety applicant and without a seed production and operation license, produced and sold the propagation material of the involved "Nan Jing 9108" for commercial purposes during the provisional protection period. This act should not be simply treated in the same manner as if the variety right holder had authorized it to implement the license; the amount of the usage fee may be appropriately increased at the court's discretion.

Considering various factors such as the amount and duration of the implementation license fee for the involved new plant variety, the variety type, and the business scale of the appellant Nantong Original Seed Farm, the first instance judgment's determination that Nantong Original Seed Farm should pay a usage fee of RMB 300,000 was not improper and was also consistent with the spirit of strengthening judicial protection of intellectual property rights for new varieties of plants.

Accordingly, the Jiangsu High People's Court, in accordance with Item (1) of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered a judgment on November 21, 2017:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
